title: Decoration for Festival: Addition and Subtraction of 2-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Addition and Subtraction of 2-Digit Numbers Class 2 Worksheet with Answers (Joyful Mathematics Chapter 6)
standard_code: Class 2, Joyful Mathematics Chapter 6: Decoration for Festival
standard_text: Addition and subtraction of 2-digit numbers with and without regrouping, using objects, number lines and stories (summary of NCERT Joyful Mathematics Class 2)
meta_desc: Class 2 Decoration for Festival worksheet (Joyful Mathematics Chapter 6): adding and subtracting 2-digit numbers, regrouping, missing numbers and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Add the tens, then the ones.
key_sub: If the ones make 10 or more, regroup into a ten.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 34 + 25: tens 30 + 20 = 50, ones 4 + 5 = 9, so 59.
  • 38 + 25: ones 8 + 5 = 13 = 1 ten 3 ones, so 63.
  • 52 − 27: take 20, then 7: 52 → 32 → 25.

Examples

Example

46 + 37

40 + 30 = 70

6 + 7 = 13

70 + 13

Answer: 83

Example

61 − 24

61 − 20 = 41

41 − 4

Answer: 37

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting the regrouped tenWrite the extra ten and add it to the tens.
Taking the smaller ones digit from the bigger52 − 27: 2 − 7 needs a ten to be broken.

faq.a: Changing 10 ones into 1 ten (or 1 ten into 10 ones) when adding or subtracting.

faq.q: Up to which numbers do Class 2 children add?

items.q: What is 62 + 2?
items.e: Add the ones: 2 + 2 = 4. The tens stay the same. 62 + 2 = 64.

items.q: What is 36 + 3?
items.e: Add the ones: 6 + 3 = 9. The tens stay the same. 36 + 3 = 39.

items.q: What is 39 − 7?
items.e: Take away the ones: 9 − 7 = 2. The tens stay the same. 39 − 7 = 32.

items.q: What is 86 − 2?
items.e: Take away the ones: 6 − 2 = 4. The tens stay the same. 86 − 2 = 84.

items.q: What is 79 − 3?
items.e: Take away the ones: 9 − 3 = 6. The tens stay the same. 79 − 3 = 76.

items.q: Use the blocks. What is 23 + 4?
items.e: Add the ones: 3 + 4 = 7. The tens stay the same. 23 + 4 = 27.

items.q: Jump to the next ten first. What is 38 + 5?
items.e: Make the next ten first. 38 + 2 = 40. 5 is 2 + 3, so add 3 more: 40 + 3 = 43.

items.q: Jump back to the ten first. What is 52 − 7?
items.e: Go back to the ten first. 52 − 2 = 50. 7 is 2 + 5, so take away 5 more: 50 − 5 = 45.

items.q: What is 61 − 7?
items.e: Go back to the ten first. 61 − 1 = 60. 7 is 1 + 6, so take away 6 more: 60 − 6 = 54.

items.q: What is 34 − 5?
items.e: Go back to the ten first. 34 − 4 = 30. 5 is 4 + 1, so take away 1 more: 30 − 1 = 29.

items.q: What is 17 + 50?
items.e: 50 is 5 tens. Add the tens: 1 ten + 5 tens = 6 tens. The ones stay the same. 17 + 50 = 67.

items.q: What is 22 + 40?
items.e: 40 is 4 tens. Add the tens: 2 tens + 4 tens = 6 tens. The ones stay the same. 22 + 40 = 62.

items.q: What is 43 − 30?
items.e: 30 is 3 tens. Take away the tens: 4 tens − 3 tens = 1 ten. The ones stay the same. 43 − 30 = 13.

items.q: What is 36 − 20?
items.e: 20 is 2 tens. Take away the tens: 3 tens − 2 tens = 1 ten. The ones stay the same. 36 − 20 = 16.

items.q: Use the blocks. What is 34 + 20?
items.e: 20 is 2 tens. Add the tens: 3 tens + 2 tens = 5 tens. The ones stay the same. 34 + 20 = 54.

items.q: Count on in tens. What is 45 + 30?
items.e: Count on 3 tens from 45: 55, 65, 75. The ones stay the same. 45 + 30 = 75.

items.q: What is 10 more than 57?
items.e: 10 more means 1 more ten. 5 tens become 6 tens. The ones stay the same: 67.

items.q: What is 10 less than 63?
items.e: 10 less means 1 fewer ten. 6 tens become 5 tens. The ones stay the same: 53.

items.q: You add 30 to 24. Which digit changes?
items.e: 30 is 3 tens, so only the tens digit changes: 24 + 30 = 54.

items.q: What is 15 + 30?
items.e: 30 is 3 tens. Add the tens: 1 ten + 3 tens = 4 tens. The ones stay the same. 15 + 30 = 45.

items.q: What is 26 + 61?
items.e: Add the tens: 20 + 60 = 80. Add the ones: 6 + 1 = 7. Then 80 + 7 = 87.

items.q: What is 31 + 26?
items.e: Add the tens: 30 + 20 = 50. Add the ones: 1 + 6 = 7. Then 50 + 7 = 57.

items.q: Add the tens, then the ones. What is 35 + 42?
items.e: Add the tens: 30 + 40 = 70. Add the ones: 5 + 2 = 7. Then 70 + 7 = 77.

items.q: Take away the tens, then the ones. What is 63 − 28?
items.e: Take away the tens first: 63 − 20 = 43. Then take away 8. Go back to the ten: 43 − 3 = 40, then 40 − 5 = 35.

items.q: Use the blocks. What is 47 + 38?
items.e: Tens: 4 + 3 = 7 tens. Ones: 7 + 8 = 15 ones. Exchange 10 ones for 1 ten: 8 tens and 5 ones. 47 + 38 = 85.

items.q: 1 ten was exchanged for 10 ones, so 54 is 4 tens and 14 ones. 26 is crossed out. What is 54 − 26?
items.e: 4 tens − 2 tens = 2 tens. 14 ones − 6 ones = 8 ones. 2 tens and 8 ones make 28. 54 − 26 = 28.

items.q: What is 48 + 25?
items.e: Add the tens: 40 + 20 = 60. Add the ones: 8 + 5 = 13. Then 60 + 13 = 73.

items.q: What is 36 + 46?
items.e: Add the tens: 30 + 40 = 70. Add the ones: 6 + 6 = 12. Then 70 + 12 = 82.

items.q: What is 28 + 47?
items.e: Add the tens: 20 + 40 = 60. Add the ones: 8 + 7 = 15. Then 60 + 15 = 75.

items.q: What is 61 − 39?
items.e: Take away the tens first: 61 − 30 = 31. Then take away 9. Go back to the ten: 31 − 1 = 30, then 30 − 8 = 22.

items.q: To add 29 + 34, Om makes a ten. He moves 1 from 34 to 29. Which is the same as 29 + 34?
items.e: 29 + 1 = 30. Then 34 − 1 = 33. So 29 + 34 = 30 + 33 = 63. Moving 1 does not change the total.

items.q: Break apart the tens and ones. Which is the same as 46 + 37?
To add 38 + 25, Manav makes a ten. He moves 2 from 25 to 38. Which is the same as 38 + 25?
items.e: 38 + 2 = 40. Then 25 − 2 = 23. So 38 + 25 = 40 + 23 = 63. Moving 2 does not change the total.

items.q: Break apart the tens and ones: 35 + 48 = 70 + ☐. What number goes in the box?
To add 19 + 57, Shreya makes a ten. She moves 1 from 57 to 19. Which is the same as 19 + 57?
items.e: 19 + 1 = 20. Then 57 − 1 = 56. So 19 + 57 = 20 + 56 = 76. Moving 1 does not change the total.

items.q: Break apart the tens and ones. Which is the same as 28 + 54?
To add 47 + 36, Rahul makes a ten. He moves 3 from 36 to 47. Which is the same as 47 + 36?
items.e: 47 + 3 = 50. Then 36 − 3 = 33. So 47 + 36 = 50 + 33 = 83. Moving 3 does not change the total.

items.q: Break apart the tens and ones: 57 + 26 = 70 + ☐. What number goes in the box?
To add 38 + 25, Neha makes a ten. She moves 2 from 25 to 38. Which is the same as 38 + 25?
items.e: 38 + 2 = 40. Then 25 − 2 = 23. So 38 + 25 = 40 + 23 = 63. Moving 2 does not change the total.

items.q: To add 47 + 36, Vivaan makes a ten. He moves 3 from 36 to 47. Which is the same as 47 + 36?
items.e: 47 + 3 = 50. Then 36 − 3 = 33. So 47 + 36 = 50 + 33 = 83. Moving 3 does not change the total.

items.q: What is 74 − 43?
items.e: Ones: 4 − 3 = 1. Tens: 7 − 4 = 3. Answer: 31. Check: 31 + 43 = 74.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Ones: 3 − 4 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 13 − 4 = 9. Tens: 5 − 3 = 2. Answer: 29. Check: 29 + 34 = 63.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Ones: 2 − 8 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 12 − 8 = 4. Tens: 2 − 1 = 1. Answer: 14. Check: 14 + 18 = 32.

items.q: What is 45 − 36?
items.e: Ones: 5 − 6 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 15 − 6 = 9. Tens: 3 − 3 = 0. Answer: 9. Check: 9 + 36 = 45.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Ones: 4 − 3 = 1. Tens: 7 − 6 = 1. Answer: 11. Check: 11 + 63 = 74.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Ones: 5 − 2 = 3. Tens: 6 − 3 = 3. Answer: 33. Check: 33 + 32 = 65.

items.q: What is 56 − 12?
items.e: Ones: 6 − 2 = 4. Tens: 5 − 1 = 4. Answer: 44. Check: 44 + 12 = 56.

items.q: What is 77 − 12?
items.e: Ones: 7 − 2 = 5. Tens: 7 − 1 = 6. Answer: 65. Check: 65 + 12 = 77.

items.q: These blocks show 52. You want to take away 27. There are only 2 ones, so you cannot take away 7 ones. What should you do first?
items.e: Trade 1 ten for 10 ones. Now there are 4 tens and 12 ones. Take away 7 ones: 12 − 7 = 5. Take away 2 tens: 4 − 2 = 2. 52 − 27 = 25.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Ones: 8 − 4 = 4. Tens: 9 − 3 = 6. Answer: 64. Check: 64 + 34 = 98.

items.q: Jump the tens, then the ones. What is 35 + 42?
Jump the tens, then the ones. What is 26 + 53?
Start at 41. Jump forward 30, then 7. Where do you land?
Jump back the tens, then the ones. What is 68 − 25?
Jump to the next ten. What is 38 + 25?
Jump to the next ten. What is 47 + 36?
Jump to the next ten. What is 56 + 28?
Jump back to the ten. What is 63 − 28?
Jump back to the ten. What is 82 − 47?
Jump back to the ten. What is 71 − 36?
Subtract.
items.e: Ones: 0 − 2 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 10 − 2 = 8. Tens: 4 − 1 = 3. Answer: 38. Check: 38 + 12 = 50. Or count up: 12 + 8 = 20, then 20 + 30 = 50. 8 + 30 = 38.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 18 + ☐ = 53
items.e: Use subtraction: 53 − 18 = ☐. Ones: 3 − 8 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 13 − 8 = 5. Tens: 4 − 1 = 3. Answer: 35. Check: 18 + 35 = 53.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 29 + ☐ = 44
items.e: Use subtraction: 44 − 29 = ☐. Ones: 4 − 9 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 14 − 9 = 5. Tens: 3 − 2 = 1. Answer: 15. Check: 29 + 15 = 44.

items.q: What is 40 − 32?
items.e: Ones: 0 − 2 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 10 − 2 = 8. Tens: 3 − 3 = 0. Answer: 8. Check: 8 + 32 = 40. Or count up: 32 + 8 = 40, then 40 + 0 = 40. 8 + 0 = 8.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 38 = 62
items.e: Use subtraction: 62 − 38 = ☐. Ones: 2 − 8 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 12 − 8 = 4. Tens: 5 − 3 = 2. Answer: 24. Check: 24 + 38 = 62.

items.q: Priya says 63 − 28 = 45. Is she right?
items.e: Check by adding: 45 + 28 = 73, not 63. So 45 is wrong. Ones: 3 − 8 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 13 − 8 = 5. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. Answer: 35. Check: 35 + 28 = 63.

items.q: Meera found 64 − 29 = 35. Which addition checks her answer?
items.e: Add the answer to the number you took away: 35 + 29 = 64. You get back 64, so the answer is right.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Ones: 0 − 9 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 10 − 9 = 1. Tens: 6 − 2 = 4. Answer: 41. Check: 41 + 29 = 70. Or count up: 29 + 1 = 30, then 30 + 40 = 70. 1 + 40 = 41.

items.q: What is 40 − 17?
items.e: Ones: 0 − 7 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 10 − 7 = 3. Tens: 3 − 1 = 2. Answer: 23. Check: 23 + 17 = 40. Or count up: 17 + 3 = 20, then 20 + 20 = 40. 3 + 20 = 23.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 26 = 63
items.e: Use subtraction: 63 − 26 = ☐. Ones: 3 − 6 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 13 − 6 = 7. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. Answer: 37. Check: 37 + 26 = 63.

items.q: Isha says 63 − 28 = 45. Is she right?
items.e: Check by adding: 45 + 28 = 73, not 63. So 45 is wrong. Ones: 3 − 8 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 13 − 8 = 5. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. Answer: 35. Check: 35 + 28 = 63.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 61 − ☐ = 15
items.e: Think: 61 take away what number leaves 15? Find 61 − 15. Ones: 1 − 5 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 11 − 5 = 6. Tens: 5 − 1 = 4. Answer: 46. Check: 61 − 46 = 15.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 33 = 61
items.e: Use subtraction: 61 − 33 = ☐. Ones: 1 − 3 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 11 − 3 = 8. Tens: 5 − 3 = 2. Answer: 28. Check: 28 + 33 = 61.

items.q: Riya found 64 − 29 = 35. Which addition checks her answer?
items.e: Add the answer to the number you took away: 35 + 29 = 64. You get back 64, so the answer is right.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 58 − ☐ = 29
items.e: Think: 58 take away what number leaves 29? Find 58 − 29. Ones: 8 − 9 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 18 − 9 = 9. Tens: 4 − 2 = 2. Answer: 29. Check: 58 − 29 = 29.

items.q: Diya says 63 − 28 = 45. Is she right?
items.e: Check by adding: 45 + 28 = 73, not 63. So 45 is wrong. Ones: 3 − 8 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 13 − 8 = 5. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. Answer: 35. Check: 35 + 28 = 63.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ + 26 = 72
items.e: Use subtraction: 72 − 26 = ☐. Ones: 2 − 6 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 12 − 6 = 6. Tens: 6 − 2 = 4. Answer: 46. Check: 46 + 26 = 72.

items.q: What is 50 − 14?
items.e: Ones: 0 − 4 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 10 − 4 = 6. Tens: 4 − 1 = 3. Answer: 36. Check: 36 + 14 = 50. Or count up: 14 + 6 = 20, then 20 + 30 = 50. 6 + 30 = 36.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Ones: 0 − 8 needs a regroup. Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: 10 − 8 = 2. Tens: 5 − 1 = 4. Answer: 42. Check: 42 + 18 = 60. Or count up: 18 + 2 = 20, then 20 + 40 = 60. 2 + 40 = 42.

items.q: Ananya found 64 − 29 = 35. Which addition checks her answer?
items.e: Add the answer to the number you took away: 35 + 29 = 64. You get back 64, so the answer is right.

items.q: There are 34 books on a shelf. Nikhil puts 5 more books on the shelf. How many books are on the shelf now?
items.e: More are added, so add. Add the ones: 4 + 5 = 9. The tens stay the same. 34 + 5 = 39.

items.q: A bus has 52 people on it. 8 people get off. How many people are still on the bus?
items.e: Some get off, so subtract. Go back to the ten first. 52 − 2 = 50. 8 is 2 + 6, so take away 6 more: 50 − 6 = 44.

items.q: Riya has 63 stickers. She gives 30 stickers to her friend. How many stickers does she have left?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. 30 is 3 tens. Take away the tens: 6 tens − 3 tens = 3 tens. The ones stay the same. 63 − 30 = 33.

items.q: One bus has 24 children on it. Another bus has 30 children. How many children are there altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. 30 is 3 tens. Add the tens: 2 tens + 3 tens = 5 tens. The ones stay the same. 24 + 30 = 54.

items.q: Kavya has 7 red pencils, 5 blue pencils and 3 green pencils. How many pencils does she have?
items.e: Add all three numbers. Look for a number bond to 10: 7 + 3 = 10. Then 10 + 5 = 15.

items.q: In a game, Shreya scores 6 points, then 8 points, then 4 points. How many points does she score altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Look for a number bond to 10: 6 + 4 = 10. Then 10 + 8 = 18.

items.q: Kabir reads 35 pages on Monday and 42 pages on Tuesday. How many pages does he read altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Add the tens: 30 + 40 = 70. Add the ones: 5 + 2 = 7. Then 70 + 7 = 77.

items.q: A farmer has 47 sheep in one field and 38 sheep in another field. How many sheep are there altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Add the tens: 40 + 30 = 70. Add the ones: 7 + 8 = 15. Then 70 + 15 = 85.

items.q: A shop has 72 apples. It sells 25 apples. How many apples are left?
items.e: Some are taken away, so subtract. Take away the tens first: 72 − 20 = 52. Then take away 5. Go back to the ten: 52 − 2 = 50, then 50 − 3 = 47.

items.q: A bus has 40 seats. 26 people are sitting down. How many seats are empty?
items.e: Take the seats with people away from all the seats, so subtract. Take away the tens first: 40 − 20 = 20. Then take away the ones: 20 − 6 = 14.

items.q: Aarav has 45 marbles. Rohan has 28 marbles. How many more marbles does Aarav have than Rohan?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. Take away the tens first: 45 − 20 = 25. Then take away 8. Go back to the ten: 25 − 5 = 20, then 20 − 3 = 17.

items.q: There are 45 people on a bus. 8 people get off. Then 20 people get on. How many people are on the bus now?
A bucket has 34 shells. Gauri finds 25 more shells. How many shells are in the bucket now?
items.e: The bar model shows two parts. Find the whole, so add. Tens: 30 + 20 = 50. Ones: 4 + 5 = 9. 50 + 9 = 59.

items.q: The canteen sold 46 icy poles at recess and 38 at lunch. How many icy poles did it sell altogether?
items.e: The bar model shows two parts. Find the whole, so add. Tens: 40 + 30 = 70. Ones: 6 + 8 = 14. 14 ones is 1 ten and 4 ones. 70 + 14 = 84.

items.q: There are 57 students on the bus. 23 students get off at the pool. How many students are still on the bus?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. Tens: 50 − 20 = 30. Ones: 7 − 3 = 4. 30 + 4 = 34.

items.q: Which number sentence finds the missing part?
items.e: The whole is 63. One part is 28. Take the part away from the whole: 63 − 28 = ?. The missing part is 35.

items.q: Which number sentence finds the whole?
items.e: The parts are 45 and 36. Put the parts together to find the whole: 45 + 36 = ?. The whole is 81.

items.q: The sausage sizzle cooked 75 sausages. 48 sausages were sold. How many sausages are left?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 75 has only 5 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 6 tens and 15 ones. Ones: 15 − 8 = 7. Tens: 6 − 4 = 2. 75 − 48 = 27.

items.q: Class 2 needs 90 cans for a recycling project. They have 54 cans. How many more cans do they need?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 90 has 0 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 8 tens and 10 ones. Ones: 10 − 4 = 6. Tens: 8 − 5 = 3. 90 − 54 = 36.

items.q: 83 people watch a race at the swimming carnival. 47 of them are students. The rest are parents. How many parents are there?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 83 has only 3 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 7 tens and 13 ones. Ones: 13 − 7 = 6. Tens: 7 − 4 = 3. 83 − 47 = 36.
